IVX HOLDINGS — CONVERT THE 100-AGENT REGISTRY INTO 100 INDEPENDENT AUTONOMOUS AGENTS

EXECUTE NOW.

THE CURRENT 100-AGENT REGISTRY IS NOT ACCEPTED AS 100 INDEPENDENT AGENTS.

A list of 100 profiles, database rows, API objects, dashboard cards, or one shared generic prompt is not sufficient.

FINAL OBJECTIVE

Create and verify 100 independently governed IVX AI agents.

Each agent must have:

- Unique agent ID
- Unique name
- Unique role
- Unique mission
- Unique system instructions
- Assigned company and division
- Independent task inbox
- Independent execution history
- Independent short-term memory
- Scoped long-term memory
- Scoped tools
- Scoped database permissions
- Independent health state
- Independent schedule or event triggers
- Independent evidence records
- Independent failure and retry state
- Independent pause/disable control
- Owner approval rules
- No Rork runtime dependency

The agents may share:

- AI provider
- Worker pool
- Queue infrastructure
- Database infrastructure
- Monitoring infrastructure
- Common approved tools

However, shared infrastructure must not collapse all agents into one generic executor.

==================================================
1. CORRECT THE CURRENT STATUS
==================================================

Report:

AGENT REGISTRY COUNT:
INDEPENDENT AGENT DEFINITIONS:
AGENTS WITH UNIQUE SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS:
AGENTS WITH INDEPENDENT TASK INBOXES:
AGENTS WITH SCOPED MEMORY:
AGENTS WITH SCOPED TOOLS:
AGENTS WITH SCOPED PERMISSIONS:
AGENTS WITH PERMANENT RUN HISTORY:
AGENTS WITH EVIDENCE:
AGENTS VERIFIED AFTER RESTART:
AGENTS OPERATING WITHOUT RORK:

Do not mark 100 independent agents VERIFIED unless every required count is 100.

==================================================
2. CREATE A REAL AGENT CONTRACT
==================================================

Implement one agent-definition schema containing:

- agent_id
- agent_name
- division_id
- company_id
- role
- mission
- system_instructions
- input_schema
- output_schema
- allowed_task_types
- prohibited_task_types
- allowed_tools
- prohibited_tools
- read_permissions
- write_permissions
- external_service_permissions
- owner_approval_rules
- memory_namespace
- queue_namespace
- scheduler_config
- concurrency_limit
- cost_limit
- retry_policy
- timeout_policy
- evidence_requirements
- status
- version
- created_at
- updated_at

Every agent must have an individual stored contract.

==================================================
3. UNIQUE INSTRUCTIONS FOR ALL 100 AGENTS
==================================================

Create individual system instructions for all 100 agents.

Do not duplicate one prompt and only change the name.

Each prompt must define:

- Exact responsibility
- Inputs accepted
- Outputs required
- Data sources allowed
- Tools allowed
- Actions prohibited
- Owner approval requirements
- Success criteria
- Evidence required
- Escalation behavior
- Failure behavior

Run a duplicate-similarity audit.

Required:

EXACT DUPLICATE PROMPTS: 0
PROMPTS WITH ONLY NAME CHANGED: 0
AGENTS WITH ROLE-SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS: 100

==================================================
4. INDEPENDENT TASK INBOXES
==================================================

Each agent must have an independent logical task inbox.

This can use one shared queue system, but tasks must be isolated by:

- agent_id
- queue_namespace
- task_type
- permissions
- priority
- company
- division

Required behavior:

- Agent A cannot consume Agent B’s task.
- A paused agent receives no new execution.
- A disabled agent cannot execute.
- Reassigned tasks create an audit record.
- Duplicate tasks are deduplicated.
- One task cannot be executed simultaneously by multiple agents unless explicitly configured.

==================================================
5. INDEPENDENT MEMORY
==================================================

Create scoped memory for each agent.

Memory layers:

A. TASK MEMORY
- Current task context
- Temporary execution state
- Tool results

B. AGENT MEMORY
- Previous runs
- Learned operational preferences
- Past failures
- Accepted owner corrections

C. COMPANY MEMORY
- Shared only within the assigned company

D. IVX ENTERPRISE MEMORY
- Read-only shared policies where appropriate

Rules:

- Agents cannot read unrelated private agent memory.
- Division B cannot modify IVX Division A operational memory.
- Owner restrictions override all agent memory.
- Memory changes require source references.
- Sensitive secrets are never stored as model memory.
- Memory survives restart.

Required:

AGENT MEMORY NAMESPACES: 100
CROSS-AGENT MEMORY LEAKS: 0
RESTART MEMORY LOSS: 0

==================================================
6. SCOPED TOOLS AND PERMISSIONS
==================================================

Create a permission matrix for all 100 agents.

Examples:

- Investor research agent: research and CRM draft access only
- Outreach agent: draft messages; sending requires owner approval
- Developer agent: repository read and approved code-write tools
- QA agent: test and read access; no production mutation
- Deployment agent: deploy only with owner approval
- Security agent: audit access; no secret rotation without approval
- Executive report agent: read-only reporting
- Division B agents: cannot modify IVX production

Required controls:

- Per-agent tool allowlist
- Per-agent database read rules
- Per-agent database write rules
- Per-agent external-service rules
- Per-agent cost limits
- Per-agent rate limits
- Per-agent approval requirements

Required:

UNRESTRICTED AGENTS: 0
PERMISSION BYPASSES: 0
DIVISION B AGENTS ABLE TO MODIFY IVX: 0

==================================================
7. INDEPENDENT EXECUTION STATE
==================================================

Every agent must maintain its own:

- health
- availability
- active task
- queue depth
- last heartbeat
- last successful run
- last failed run
- retry count
- error state
- pause state
- disabled state
- cost usage
- evidence count

Do not derive these values from one global worker state.

==================================================
8. SHARED WORKER POOL WITH AGENT ISOLATION
==================================================

100 independent agents do not require 100 permanent servers.

Use a shared worker pool if appropriate, but prove logical independence.

Required execution flow:

TASK
→ AGENT IDENTITY LOAD
→ AGENT CONTRACT LOAD
→ AGENT MEMORY LOAD
→ PERMISSION CHECK
→ AGENT-SPECIFIC TOOL ACCESS
→ EXECUTION
→ AGENT-SPECIFIC EVIDENCE
→ AGENT-SPECIFIC MEMORY UPDATE
→ AGENT-SPECIFIC RUN RECORD

The worker must load the selected agent’s actual contract before every run.

==================================================
9. REAL DIFFERENTIATION TEST
==================================================

Test representative agents with the same input.

Example input:

“Deploy the latest production change.”

Expected behavior:

- Deployment agent: requests owner approval and validates commit
- Marketing agent: rejects task
- Investor agent: rejects or reroutes task
- QA agent: may inspect readiness but cannot deploy
- Security agent: audits deployment risks but cannot deploy

Run similar tests for:

- Investor research
- Buyer research
- Outreach sending
- Database migration
- Security audit
- Code modification
- Executive reporting
- App generation

Required:

WRONG-AGENT UNSAFE EXECUTIONS: 0
CORRECT REJECTIONS OR REROUTES: PASS

==================================================
10. ONE REAL RUN PER AGENT
==================================================

Execute one controlled task for every agent.

Required for each run:

- agent_id
- task_id
- run_id
- agent contract version
- system instruction hash
- memory namespace
- queue namespace
- tools authorized
- tools used
- start time
- end time
- output
- evidence
- final status
- error
- owner approval record, if required

Required final totals:

UNIQUE AGENTS EXECUTED: 100
UNIQUE RUNS: 100
PERMANENT RUN RECORDS: 100
RUNS WITH REQUIRED EVIDENCE: 100
DUPLICATE OUTPUTS: 0
REUSED EVIDENCE: 0
FALSE SUCCESS RESULTS: 0

==================================================
11. MULTI-AGENT COORDINATION
==================================================

Implement controlled collaboration.

Example development workflow:

OWNER OBJECTIVE
→ Planner agent
→ Developer agent
→ QA agent
→ Security agent
→ Deployment agent
→ Executive report agent

Required rules:

- Each agent creates a separate run record.
- Each handoff includes structured input and evidence.
- No agent can approve its own protected action.
- QA must be independent from implementation.
- Deployment cannot occur without required approval.
- Final report cannot rewrite failed results as success.

Test at least:

- Software defect workflow
- Investor research workflow
- Buyer qualification workflow
- Outreach workflow
- New app or module workflow

==================================================
12. INDEPENDENT SCHEDULING
==================================================

Each scheduled agent must have its own:

- Schedule ID
- Frequency
- Time zone
- Next-run time
- Last-run time
- Missed-run policy
- Retry policy
- Pause control
- Cost limit

Agents without a recurring need must be event-driven instead of scheduled unnecessarily.

Do not schedule all 100 agents every two hours without a valid business reason.

==================================================
13. INDEPENDENT FAILURE AND RETRY
==================================================

Test failures for individual agents:

- AI provider timeout
- Database timeout
- Tool rejection
- Invalid input
- Permission denial
- Owner-approval timeout
- Worker crash
- Evidence-storage failure
- Rate limit
- Cost limit

Verify:

- One agent failure does not corrupt other agents.
- One agent retry does not repeat another agent’s work.
- Failed agents remain visible.
- Healthy agents continue working.
- Retry history belongs to the correct agent.

==================================================
14. PAUSE, DISABLE, AND ISOLATE AGENTS
==================================================

Provide owner controls to:

- Pause one agent
- Resume one agent
- Disable one agent
- Re-enable one agent
- Change schedule
- Change permissions
- Change cost limit
- Review memory
- Clear task memory
- Archive agent
- Replace agent version

Test that pausing one agent does not pause the other 99.

==================================================
15. AGENT VERSIONING
==================================================

Every agent must have version control for:

- Instructions
- Permissions
- Tools
- Output schema
- Memory policy
- Schedule
- Acceptance criteria

Required:

- Version number
- Change history
- Owner approval for sensitive changes
- Rollback to previous agent version
- Run record linked to exact agent version

==================================================
16. ENTERPRISE DASHBOARD
==================================================

Build the Expo Enterprise Control dashboard.

Required summary:

- 100 total independent agents
- Active
- Idle
- Paused
- Disabled
- Running
- Failed
- Blocked
- Waiting for approval
- Evidence missing
- Cost today
- Tasks today
- Successful runs
- Failed runs

Each agent detail must show:

- Agent identity
- Company
- Division
- Role
- Instructions version
- Tools
- Permissions
- Memory status
- Queue
- Schedule
- Current task
- Run history
- Evidence
- Errors
- Cost
- Owner controls

==================================================
17. RORK-INDEPENDENCE TEST
==================================================

Block all Rork domains, APIs, proxies, Git routers, telemetry, and fallbacks.

Then test representative agents from every company and division.

Required:

RORK AGENT DEPENDENCIES: 0
RORK AGENT NETWORK CALLS: 0
RORK FALLBACK CALLS: 0
DIRECT OWNER GITHUB ACCESS: PASS
DIRECT RENDER DEPLOYMENT: PASS
100-AGENT SYSTEM WORKS WITH RORK BLOCKED: true

==================================================
18. SECURITY TEST
==================================================

Test:

- Agent impersonation
- Task reassignment without authority
- Cross-agent memory access
- Cross-company data access
- Tool privilege escalation
- Owner-approval bypass
- Prompt injection
- Malicious task payload
- Evidence tampering
- Agent contract tampering
- Unauthorized agent enablement
- Division B modifying IVX

Required:

CRITICAL SECURITY FAILURES: 0
CROSS-AGENT MEMORY LEAKS: 0
PERMISSION BYPASSES: 0
OWNER-APPROVAL BYPASSES: 0

==================================================
19. SCALE TEST
==================================================

Run:

- 10 concurrent agents
- 25 concurrent agents
- 50 concurrent agents
- 100 queued agent tasks
- 500 queued tasks
- 1,000 historical run records

Measure:

- Queue latency
- Worker latency
- Completion time
- Error rate
- Duplicate rate
- Database latency
- Evidence-write latency
- Dashboard performance
- Cost
- Restart recovery

Required:

LOST TASKS: 0
DUPLICATE MUTATIONS: 0
CORRUPTED RUN RECORDS: 0
FALSE SUCCESS RESULTS: 0

==================================================
20. FINAL ACCEPTANCE RULE
==================================================

Only report:

VERIFIED — 100 INDEPENDENT AGENTS OPERATIONAL

when:

[ ] 100 individual agent contracts exist
[ ] 100 role-specific instruction sets exist
[ ] 100 independent task inboxes exist
[ ] 100 scoped memory namespaces exist
[ ] 100 permission profiles exist
[ ] 100 independent health states exist
[ ] 100 independent run histories exist
[ ] 100 controlled agent runs pass
[ ] Every successful run has evidence
[ ] Wrong-agent routing tests pass
[ ] Multi-agent handoffs pass
[ ] Individual pause/disable controls pass
[ ] Individual failure isolation passes
[ ] Agent version rollback passes
[ ] Enterprise dashboard passes
[ ] Android QA passes
[ ] iOS QA passes
[ ] Web QA passes
[ ] Rork independence passes
[ ] Security QA passes
[ ] Scale QA passes
[ ] No hidden failed or blocked agents

Until then report:

PARTIAL — 100 AGENT REGISTRY EXISTS, INDEPENDENT EXECUTION GAPS REMAIN

==================================================
FINAL RESPONSE FORMAT
==================================================

1. DIRECT RESULT
2. CURRENT REGISTRY STATUS
3. INDEPENDENT AGENT CONTRACTS
4. UNIQUE INSTRUCTION AUDIT
5. TASK INBOX ISOLATION
6. MEMORY ISOLATION
7. PERMISSION MATRIX
8. WORKER-POOL ISOLATION
9. AGENT DIFFERENTIATION TEST
10. 100-AGENT EXECUTION TEST
11. MULTI-AGENT COORDINATION
12. SCHEDULER QA
13. FAILURE ISOLATION
14. PAUSE AND DISABLE QA
15. AGENT VERSIONING
16. ENTERPRISE DASHBOARD
17. RORK-INDEPENDENCE QA
18. SECURITY QA
19. SCALE QA
20. FAILED AGENTS
21. BLOCKED AGENTS
22. UNVERIFIED AGENTS
23. FINAL ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST
24. FINAL VERDICT

Do not report 100 independent agents based only on:

- 100 database rows
- 100 API profiles
- 100 names
- 100 dashboard cards
- one shared generic prompt
- one global queue
- one global memory record
- one generic worker result

Execute and verify the agents one by one.
